messages.author: 20c6dbb46920d12c
messages.subject: Work around for facet error?
parts:
Has anyone suggested a work around for the bug in facet grid, in which ties are not counted?

Or, has the bug been fixed?

Or, is my understanding of the bug incorrect?

Thanks as always for the help.

Adam

messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: Work around for facet error?
parts:
On 4/30/2012 1:47 PM, Adam Loveland wrote:
> Has anyone suggested a work around for the bug in facet grid, in which
> ties are not counted?

If your data frame is DF, then add a non-duplicated column

DF$dummy <- seq(length=nrow(DF))

(assuming, of course, you don't already have a column named dummy)
> Or, has the bug been fixed?

Yes, in the development version which will become 0.9.1
https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/443

> Or, is my understanding of the bug incorrect?
>
> Thanks as always for the help.
>
> Adam

--
Brian S. Diggs, PhD
Senior Research Associate, Department of Surgery
Oregon Health & Science University

messages.subject: Re: Work around for facet error?
parts:
On 4/30/2012 5:35 PM, Adam Loveland wrote:
> Thanks very much. So the bug applies to duplicate records, then, not
> duplicate values necessarily? Just making sure. Thanks again.

Yes. unique() was being called on a data.frame when it shouldn't have
been. The data.frame was an augmented version of the original data
(additional columns for internal ggplot-ish things). So making the
original data have no duplicated rows is sufficient to make the
augmented data also have no duplicated rows and thus make unique() an
effective no-op on that data.frame.
